Nima moved to a new town last year. At first he missed his old friends. One afternoon his cousin Laleh invited him to a board-game club. He enjoyed solving puzzles there and met two friendly classmates.

Now Nima visits the club every Friday. His younger sister sometimes joins him. He still writes to his old friends, and he wants to invite them to the club during the holidays.

The community garden · original fictional model

The students have decided to turn an empty corner of their school into a garden. On Saturday they are going to bring seeds and small tools. Their teacher has already arranged the tables.

“I think we’ll grow plenty of vegetables,” says Eda. Her friend notices a heavy bag and offers, “I’ll carry that.” They hope the garden will become a quiet place for reading, but they know they will have to look after it.

The missing model · original fictional model

At six o’clock, Roya was making a cardboard model in the living room. Her brother was washing a cup in the kitchen. When the doorbell rang, Roya put the model on a shelf and went downstairs.

Later she could not find it. She looked under the table and behind the sofa. Then her brother arrived with the model. He had moved it to a dry cupboard because water was dripping from a plant above the shelf.

The library visit · original fictional model

Tara and Elvin are meeting at the station on Saturday at ten. They have booked places at a model-making workshop in the town library. From the station they will walk along Oak Road, turn left at the fountain and cross a small bridge. The library is next to the museum.

Elvin thought he had lost the booking message, but Tara found it in his diary. “Nothing has gone wrong,” she said. They are bringing a cardboard box and some coloured paper.

The reuse club · original fictional model

Ari’s class has started a reuse club. They have collected clean cardboard boxes and made storage trays. Last Tuesday they displayed their work in the school hall. Ari has never spoken to a large group before, but he has agreed to introduce the club next week.

His friend Mina has just sent him a short practice recording. He has listened to it twice. They are going to practise together on Friday, and Ari feels proud of the work they have done.

The borrowed camera · original fictional model

Pelin borrowed her cousin’s camera for the school exhibition. The club had three rules: members must sign equipment out, must not leave it outdoors, and do not have to bring their own camera. Pelin wrote her name in the book before leaving.

At home she could not switch the camera on. She looked for the battery in the bag and found it in a small pocket. She put it back in the camera and tried it out. The screen lit up. She sent her cousin a message to say that everything was working.
